thread:
Kelsey (Support): Samir from AcmeMobile reports a flurry of 429s after moving traffic to a Dedicated reserved pool this morning. Customer says auth is succeeding but responses are failing with rate_limit_exceeded. They pasted an example response and some client traces — sharing here to triage.

Samir (Customer): i've attached the curl + response we get. it works for a bit then starts returning 429 JSON. no TTL issue on tokens. we only started hitting this after switching to dedicated (rp-9f3).

Samir (Customer): ```
$ curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxxx" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"rw-1-large","input":"hey"}' 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60/min
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 84

{"error":{"type":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"Rate limit exceeded for key"}}
```

Kelsey (Support): Thanks — that header set is useful. Can you confirm if you're using a single API key across many clients or multiple keys? Also, did you pin a model variant or rely on smart routing?

Samir (Customer): single key for now. traffic pattern: normal app traffic + nightly batch that started at 02:00 UTC. batch does ~5k small requests over 10 minutes. didn't see this on hosted. switched to rp-9f3 on dedicated to lower latency.

Devon (SRE): pinging in. On Dedicated we have two places that enforce limits: the per-key rate limiter (global for the account) and the reserved-pool throughput cap (the pool config + per-worker token/sec budget). If the X-RateLimit-Limit header shows 60/min that's the per-key plan limit — sounds like the customer is still hitting account-level throttle, not necessarily pool internal.

Devon (SRE): Can you run `redwoodctl pool describe --id rp-9f3` and paste the output? Also check `redwoodctl key describe --key sk-live-xxxx` to see plan-level quotas.

Samir (Customer): ran both. output below (sanitized):

```
$ redwoodctl pool describe --id rp-9f3
id: rp-9f3
region: us-west-2
model_profiles: [rw-1-large]
pool_throughput_cap: 250 token/s
pool_burst_window: 60s
pool_burst_tokens: 15000
reserved_accounts: [acct-77]

$ redwoodctl key describe --key sk-live-xxxx
key_id: sk-live-xxxx
plan: team-standard
per_minute_limit: 60
per_hour_limit: 3000
```

Alex (Eng): that confirms it — the plan-level per_minute_limit is 60/min. On hosted that map would've been bumped automatically for dedicated customers during onboarding, but looks like this account kept the default key quota after the pool migration. The rate-limit headers are emitted by the API gateway before pool admission.

Devon (SRE): short-term mitigation: we can either bump the key quota for the customer (increase per_minute_limit) or implement a temporary API key override tied to the reserved pool. Long-term we should ensure onboarding script for Dedicated updates key quotas or proxies rate limits to pool-level caps.

Kelsey (Support): Samir, would you prefer we bump the key limits now while we follow up on infra fix? Also, can you share a short repro we can run from our side to verify?

Samir (Customer): yes pls bump. repro is simple loop hitting the same key at ~80 rps for 30s, you'll see 429 after the minute threshold. here's a tiny script:```
for i in $(seq 1 120); do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxxx" -d '{"model":"rw-1-large","input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done
wait
```

rate-limiter-bot: Notice: quota-override-request created (req-id: qov-2026). Automated checks: key valid, no suspicious spikes.

Devon (SRE): I will bump the key quota to 1200/min temporarily and create a ticket to reconcile plan and pool quotas. Applying now..

Devon (SRE): done. `key.per_minute_limit` set to 1200 for sk-live-xxxx (temp until 2026-03-15T08:00:00Z). Please retry.

Samir (Customer): re-ran test, no 429s during the same window. latency looks good. thanks!

Alex (Eng): while this is resolved for the immediate hit, we should add an onboarding step: when migrating an account to Dedicated reserved pools, auto-adjust API-key rate limits to be min(plan_limit * 10, pool_throughput_cap * X) or something sane. Also add an alert rule when X-RateLimit-Remaining == 0 for any key in Dedicated pools to catch this proactively.

Maria (Billing): flagged for a brief internal check — increasing key quota raises potential spend. Samir, do you want us to set a hard spend cap or alert for the nighttime batch?

Samir (Customer): pls add spend alert + keep the temporary quota. we'll also throttle the batch job on our side ASAP. thanks everyone.

Kelsey (Support): Next steps for us: (1) leave the quota bump in place for 48h, (2) create an onboarding automation ticket for quota alignment, (3) add an alert runbook so support can catch these before customer notices. I'll open the follow-up tickets and ping product for the onboarding change.

Devon (SRE): filing infra ticket: INFRA-6221 "Sync API key quotas with Dedicated reserved pool on migration". Assigning to eng-runtime.

Alex (Eng): also adding small doc snippet for customers: "If you run bursty batch jobs, create a secondary key or reserve a burst window in the pool config — don't rely on a single low-plan key".

Kelsey (Support): marking resolved for now since 429s stopped after quota bump. Will follow up on tickets and schedule a 1:1 with Samir to discuss right-sizing. :white_check_mark:

Samir (Customer): really appreciate the fast turnaround.

rate-limiter-bot: Closed: qov-2026 (quota override applied and verified).

Kelsey (Support): action items:
- Support: create ticket SUP-9813 for customer follow-up
- Eng-runtime: INFRA-6221 (quota sync automation)
- SRE: add alert when X-RateLimit-Remaining == 0 for Dedicated pool keys
- Billing: add spend-alert for acct-77

Kelsey (Support): tagging this resolved in channel, will update thread after onboarding automation PR lands. :thumbsup:
